Job Summary: The Electrical Apprentice is responsible for assisting the Electrical Journeyman or Master Electrician with the installation of electrical equipment and materials.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities: 
•    Assist with the installation of electrical equipment, including cabinets, meters, sub-metering, conduit, and wiring
•    Adhere to all Company, customer, and regulatory safety policies, including OSHA requirements and proper use of PPE
•    Read and interpret basic electrical drawings and schematics as directed
•    Utilize electrical testing equipment as required
•    Assist with site preparation, grounding, bonding, and basic troubleshooting under supervision
•    Maintain a clean and orderly work environment 
•    Complete all required Company documentation 
•    Other duties as assigned

Qualifications: To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty mentioned satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skills, and/or ability required.

Education: High school diploma, general education degree (G.E.D.), or related trade school education

Experience: 
•    One to two years of electrical experience 
•    Less than one-year of wireless telecommunications industry experience 
•    Ability to operate hand and power tools
•    Knowledge of electrical codes and licensing
•    Must have or obtain and maintain OSHA Construction 10-hour Safety Training Card
•    Must have or obtain and maintain First Aid and CPR certification
•    Must have or obtain and maintain RF Radiation Safety & Awareness certification
•    Knowledge of safety procedures and regulations, including OSHA standards and proper use of personal protective equipment (PPE)
•    Understanding of conduit bending and wire pulling techniques
•    Ability to measure, cut, and assemble electrical conduit and wiring
•    Willingness to learn and follow instructions related to electrical codes and standards

Technical Skills:
•    Computer and Microsoft Office proficiency
•    Basic understanding of electrical systems, components, and wiring methods
•    Ability to assist in installing, repairing, and maintaining electrical systems under the supervision of a licensed electrician
•    Familiarity with hand and power tools commonly used in electrical work (e.g., wire strippers, drills, multimeters)
•    Ability to read and interpret simple blueprints and diagrams with guidance
•    Basic troubleshooting skills to identify and report issues to senior electricians
•    Basic math skills for measuring, calculating loads, and determining material needs
•    Familiarity with lockout/tagout procedures and safe work practices

Soft Skills:
•    Consistently demonstrates reliability, punctuality, and a strong commitment to completing work safely, efficiently, and to a high standard of quality 
•    Works effectively as part of a team; supports a positive and collaborative work environment 
•    Follows instructions and accepts direction from licensed electricians and supervisors
•    Maintains attention to detail when performing work and completing documentation
•    Communicates clearly to report issues, ask questions, and coordinate work activitiesManages time effectively to complete assigned tasks safely and efficiently
•    Maintains awareness of surroundings and safety risks while working with heavy equipment 
•    Takes accountability for tools, materials, and assigned responsibilities 

Physical Requirements: 
•    Must be able to pass pre-employment screening that includes background and drug testing
•    Must have a valid driver’s license and a driving record that meets Company requirements
•    Ability to lift, carry, push, and pull up to 75 pounds regularly 
•    Ability to stoop, kneel, crouch, crawl, reach, and grasp materials and tools with both hands
•    Ability to work long hours in outdoor environments, including extreme weather conditions such as heat, cold, rain, wind, or snow 
•    Ability to stand, walk, and perform physically demanding tasks for extended periods of time 
•    Ability to wear the required personal protective equipment (PPE), including fall protection, hard hat, safety glasses, and gloves
•    Comfortable working in confined spaces and at varying elevations 
•    Ability to work long and unpredictable hours 
•    Ability to travel away from home up to 75% of the time, including weekends and extended travel. Travel includes local site travel or national travel depending on business needs.
